title: The organ grinder and early ragtime tunes
summary: Laine says no band played rag when he was eight, but kids whistled it and an organ grinder's ragged tune was paid for by neighborhood men.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: No, 94. She kept track of all the business. 95. Let me ask you this. You said you were about eight years old when you heard your first rag. Well, around that, yes. Did you... It was a band that played it? Was it a regular professional band that played it? No, I never heard no band play it now. Well, now... No. No. Was somebody whistling it? Or singing it? Was somebody singing it or what?

Plenty of people whistling. Plenty of the kids whistling and different things. Now, there used to be an organ grinder. They used to stop at the corner. That's the time they had them organs to throw you on their back, you know. And they had a tune in there. I can't remember that tune. They used to... That tune used to rag the mischief out of it.
Is that right? That organ grinder?

Organ grinder. And brother, them boys around the corner, even kids around the corner, big men, I'm cheeky and I'm... They'd have that organ grinder stand there and give them as high as 50, 60 cents to stay there and play that tune. Is that right? Yeah.
